newsitem.title: USA: Harcourt in talks to buy National Education.
newsitem.headline: Harcourt in talks to buy National Education.

text.p: Publisher and speciality retailer Harcourt General Inc. sweetened its cash offer for National Education Corp. to about $800 million and said it was in talks with the company, which struck a deal in March to be acquired by Sylvan Learning Systems.
Harcourt on April 16 offered $19.50 a share, or $740 million, for National Education, whose products include correspondence courses and educational textbooks.
If a deal to acquire Irvine, Calif.-based National Education goes through, Harcourt would raise the $19.50 offer to $21, Harcourt General said Wednesday.
"If these negotiations are not successful, Harcourt General will continue its offer to purchase all NEC shares at $19.50 per share," Chestnut Hill, Mass.-based Harcourt said in a statement.

Sylvan Learning Systems in March struck a stock deal under which National Education shareholders would receive 0.58 share of Sylvan for each share held. Initially valued at $750 million, the value of the deal had slipped to $647 million by the time Harcourt made its offer.
Sylvan stock was up $1.375 to $31.50 in afternoon trading on the Nasdaq, raising the offer's value to $676 million.
National Education edged up 25 cents to $20.50, while Harcourt General dropped 87.5 cents to $45.375 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Harcourt General owns publishers Harcourt Brace & Co.; Holt, Rinehart and Winston; The Psychological Corp. and WB Saunders. It also has a 53 percent stake in the Neiman Marcus Group, which operates the upscale Neiman Marcus and Bergdorf Goodman department stores.

Baltimore-based Sylvan Learning Systems provides educational services in the United States, Canada, France, Germany and seven other countries. It has 517 franchised and company-owned learning centres, 29 public and private school-based learning centres and 14 centres at workplaces.
